minor_characters.name: Albert (lift-boy/errand-runner)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Helps Tuppence at South Audley Mansions, runs messages, plays greengrocer’s boy, warns of Mrs. Vandemeyer’s departure, and assists Tommy’s Gatehouse stakeout (Ch 010, 012–013, 024).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His errands and warnings can be reassigned to anonymous messengers or folded into narration without affecting the core plot.

minor_characters.name: Annie (Mrs. Vandemeyer’s maid)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Gossips to Tuppence about the household and exits in a huff as Tuppence takes the job (Ch 010).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her function is purely expository and can be summarized in a sentence of narration.

minor_characters.name: Cook at Mrs. Vandemeyer’s
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Kitchen presence who fears the mistress and chats briefly with Tuppence (Ch 010–011).
minor_characters.reason_removable: She contributes atmosphere only and no plot turns depend on her.

minor_characters.name: Hall porter at South Audley Mansions
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Seen supervising Albert and opening doors during Tuppence’s maid infiltration (Ch 010).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He adds building color but no story beat hinges on him.

minor_characters.name: Henry (page at the Ritz)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Delivers Tuppence’s telegram and casually reports her sudden departure (Ch 019).
minor_characters.reason_removable: A desk clerk or brief narration can convey the same information with fewer moving parts.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Sweeny (caretaker of the Moat House)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Loans the key and confirms the house has stood empty when Tommy and Julius search it (Ch 019).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her scene is part of a detour that can be summarized or elided without loss to the main arc.

minor_characters.name: George (Julius’s chauffeur)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Drives during Julius’s kidnapping of Kramenin and the Gatehouse rescue (Ch 025).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His driving can remain offstage; naming and character beats are unnecessary.

minor_characters.name: Butler and footman at Gatehouse
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Appear fleetingly as staff when Julius bluffs Kramenin’s ‘order’ to release the girls (Ch 025).
minor_characters.reason_removable: They are nameless obstacles; their actions can be compressed to ‘house staff.’

minor_characters.name: Sir William Beresford
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Tommy’s crusty uncle who reconciles and offers a home/allowance during the Savoy coda (Ch 028–029).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His reconciliation subplot is peripheral to the spy plot and themes and can be cut cleanly.

minor_characters.name: American Ambassador
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Attends the Savoy supper and invites Jane to the Embassy (Ch 028).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Diplomatic kudos can be implied via Mr. Carter’s toast; his presence is not structurally needed.

minor_characters.name: Dr. Roylance
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Sir James’s doctor friend in Manchester who houses Jane after her street accident (Ch 020).
minor_characters.reason_removable: The ‘kindly doctor’ function can be left unnamed or summarized during Jane’s reveal without changing events.

minor_characters.name: Inspector Japp (name-only)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Referenced on a calling card mix‑up during the photograph theft (Ch 006–007).
minor_characters.reason_removable: This name-drop adds no plot leverage and can be omitted.

minor_characters.name: Greengrocer’s boy / carter
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Helps Albert with a ruse and later delivers Jane’s roadside note to Tommy (Ch 024).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Anonymous helpers can be elided; both notes can be handed off in narration.

minor_characters.name: Number 14 (henchman)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A named thug who helps bind Tommy in Soho (Ch 010, 018).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He can be collapsed into ‘a henchman’ without losing clarity or stakes.

subplots.name: Julius’s impulsive proposal to Tuppence
subplots.reason_removable: This comic feint toward a triangle is resolved immediately and does not alter later pairings or stakes.

subplots.name: Tommy’s inheritance reconciliation with Sir William
subplots.reason_removable: A feel‑good tag unrelated to the conspiracy; cutting it keeps the denouement focused on the case’s end and the partners’ future.

subplots.name: The Moat House (Ebury) caretaker detour
subplots.reason_removable: The empty‑house search and caretaker interview add delay without changing outcomes; Tuppence’s abduction can be reported without the village interlude.

subplots.name: Albert’s disguises and ‘frog‑croak’ signal caper
subplots.reason_removable: These light capers can be summarized as “Tommy used a messenger to stake out the house,” preserving momentum.

subplots.name: Rolls‑Royce shopping and dollars-as-sledgehammer vignette
subplots.reason_removable: It establishes Julius’s wealth comically but can be implied elsewhere with no effect on plot or theme.

subplots.name: Full Savoy supper guest‑list and matchmaking coda
subplots.reason_removable: The lengthy dinner scene can be compressed to Mr. Carter’s toast and the partners’ engagement without the parade of attendees and banter.

digressions.topic: Extended money-and-marriage banter and Tuppence’s ‘abridged biography’ at Lyons
digressions.reason_removable: Lengthy comic patter can be trimmed to their joblessness and decision to form the Young Adventurers, keeping pace brisk.

digressions.topic: Tommy’s meta‑commentary on ‘how to follow people’ in fiction vs. real streets
digressions.reason_removable: Amusing aside that slows the chase without revealing character or moving the plot.

digressions.topic: Soho room filth and peep‑hole set‑dressing in excess
digressions.reason_removable: Atmosphere repeats can be tightened once the danger layout (no window, thick door, peep‑hole) is established.

digressions.topic: Julius’s extravagant car‑buying anecdote and hotel comedy
digressions.reason_removable: Comic business about money and service adds flavor but not story beats.

digressions.topic: Julius’s tall tales (Arizona, Rockies) while menacing Kramenin
digressions.reason_removable: The scare tactic works without the embellished yarns; condensing keeps the rescue taut.

digressions.topic: Lavish Savoy supper menu, flowers, and long guest introductions
digressions.reason_removable: Ornate description can be reduced to Mr. Carter’s toast and brief recognition to keep the denouement sleek.

digressions.topic: Long quotations from Sir James’s diary
digressions.reason_removable: His motive and dual life can be summarized in a few lines once his identity as Mr. Brown is revealed.

digressions.topic: Step‑by‑step travelogue of trains, missed turns, and small‑talk in the Ebury search
digressions.reason_removable: A detour that can be summarized as a fruitless chase without scenic detail.
